chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn 'Abdah who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the loan that brings benefit, and he said, 'The best loan is the one that brings benefit.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (title of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْقَرْضِ: Loan (a sum of money or goods given to another with the expectation of return)

ai.seo_question: Is a loan that yields benefit considered valid in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) explicitly validates the concept of *qard al-jarrah* (loan with benefit), challenging the stricter view that loans must be purely gratuitous to avoid riba. By designating the beneficial loan as the 'best,' the Imam underscores the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence, allowing lenders to receive non-exploitative benefits such as gifts or services in return for the loan.
